tasks.short: Record weather and fuel moisture during the burn, walk the burned area, analyze burn conditions and results, write the postburn report, and send it to the land manager.

steps.what: Fire captain takes fuel moisture readings during the burn and writes them down: on paper today, in a tablet form after the change
Fire captain reads and writes down wind, humidity and temperature during the burn: by hand today; after the change the portable weather station logs them and the captain checks the log is running
Fire captain walks the burned area to assess results
Fire captain puts the logged weather and fuel moisture readings beside the burn plan's weather limits
Fire captain analyzes burn conditions and results against the burn plan
Fire captain prepares the postburn report

loop.input: The burn plan, the logged weather and fuel moisture readings, the mapped burned area and the captain's notes.
loop.output: A draft postburn report in the region's template.
loop.check: Code checks every reading, time and area in the text matches the logged data and lists any plan objective without a result. The captain reads each drafted statement about results against their own analysis and site notes, and rewrites or removes any statement the analysis does not support; results the captain is unsure of are written by hand.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the captain approves, or after two failed redrafts the captain writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: What went well and what to change needs prose; a template only fills in the numbers.

steps.what: Fire captain checks the final postburn report: readings, results against each objective, and the land manager it goes to
Fire captain sends the checked postburn report to the land manager: by e-mail with a cover note today, by one send from the document system after the change

tasks.design: A portable weather station logs wind, humidity and temperature during the burn, so the captain stops reading and writing weather by hand; the captain still takes fuel moisture readings and enters them in a form on the tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}). The burned perimeter is walked with the tablet's GPS. A bounded step drafts the postburn report from the plan, the logged readings and the captain's notes; code checks every number and the captain reads each statement about results against their own analysis and edits. The captain checks the final report and its recipient, then sends it to the land manager. Walking the area and judging results stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written on paper and reports typed from scratch weeks later.
tasks.enabler_now: Portable weather stations log readings; tablets map perimeters; language models draft reports from structured data.
tasks.still_hard: Effects on vegetation show only months later.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a patchy burn was the weather or the crew's ignition pattern.
tasks.altitude: The captain edits reports instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive before the next burn is planned.

evidence.claim: Portable weather stations log readings; language models can draft reports from structured data with numbers checked by code.

assumptions: Boundary: from the burn plan to the report sent; vegetation monitoring in later years is outside.
Input contract: burn plan from the region; readings from the weather station; fallback is paper and typing.

Walking the area, judging results, taking fuel moisture readings (a first record) and the check before sending keep their full time. s1w keeps 20 for checking the station log; s3 keeps 35 for reading the readings against the limits; s5 keeps 75 because readings and objectives fill in and the captain writes the analysis; sending keeps 25.
No personal data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted report does the captain change?

already_counted.description: Fire captain edits and approves the drafted report.

incremental.description: Fire captain sets up and checks the weather station before the burn.

approvals.approved_version: The final postburn report exactly as checked by the captain in s5c, sent once to the land manager named in the burn plan; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the region has too few stations, so on about half of burns the captain reads weather by hand and lines it up (16.1); high: a station at every burn as designed (23.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the inspection from the permit file, take part in inspections of properties, supervise the inspectors, record findings, decide on compliance and check the findings letter, and send it to the owner.

steps.what: Fire captain prepares the inspection from the permit file and earlier findings
Fire captain participates in the inspection of properties for compliance with fire codes
Fire captain supervises the inspectors on site
Fire captain records findings on site: on the paper checklist today, on the tablet checklist with photos after the change
Fire captain types up the paper checklist into the findings record
Fire captain decides on compliance for each finding
Fire captain checks the final findings letter: each finding, its code article, the decision and the owner's address
Fire captain sends the checked findings letter to the property owner: printed and posted today, sent from the inspection app after the change

tasks.design: The inspection app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the permit, drawings and earlier findings per address, and the checklist on the tablet names the code article behind each item, so findings are recorded once on site with photos. The findings letter fills from the recorded items with their articles. The captain decides on compliance, checks the final letter and the owner's address, and sends it from the app. Inspecting, supervising inspectors and deciding stay with the captain; inspection times are not used to rate inspectors.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permit files sat in archives, findings went on paper and letters were typed afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Inspection apps with checklists linked to code articles are common in safety regions and municipalities.
tasks.still_hard: Older buildings rarely match their drawings.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a blocked escape route is a habit, not an accident.

reach.learn: Whether letters go out the same week.

evidence.claim: Inspection apps can show permit files and link checklist items to code articles.
Systems that can monitor staff, such as time-stamped inspection logs, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the inspection planning to the letter sent; enforcement proceedings are outside.
Input contract: permit files from the municipality's archive; checklists kept by the region; fallback is paper.

Inspecting, supervising, recording findings on site (a first record), deciding and checking the letter keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because the file is on one screen and reading it stays; typing up keeps 10 for inspections where the tablet cannot be used; sending keeps 20.
Owners receive the letter as they do today; no added owner time.
research_questions: Do repeat inspections find fewer open items?

incremental.description: Fire captain reports outdated checklist items.

approvals.approved_version: The findings letter with findings, code articles and compliance decision exactly as checked by the captain in s5c, sent once to the property owner at the address in the permit file; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half of inspections are still recorded on paper and typed up (14.5); high: the tablet is used at nearly every inspection (18.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the burn plan, coordinate with the land manager, neighbours and dispatch centre, decide go or no-go on the day, notify those involved, and direct and supervise the burn.

steps.what: Fire captain plans prescribed burn projects in a burn plan
Fire captain coordinates with the land manager, neighbours and the dispatch centre
Fire captain decides go or no-go on the day from the weather forecast
Fire captain checks the start message: burn unit, start time, the captain's contact number and the recipients on the list
Fire captain tells the dispatch centre, land manager and neighbours that the burn starts: by phone today, by one message to the burn's contact list after the change
Fire captain directs and supervises the prescribed burn

tasks.design: Burn plans start from the region's template ({DOCS}) with map, objectives, weather limits and crew pre-filled from the last burn of that unit. A shared contact list holds the land manager, neighbours and dispatch centre; once the captain decides go and checks the start message and its recipients, one message tells all of them the burn starts. Agreeing with the land manager, deciding go or no-go and directing the burn stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were written from scratch and everyone was phoned on the morning of the burn.
tasks.enabler_now: Plan templates and group messages are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: The weather window can close within an hour.
tasks.human_edge: Calling off a burn when the wind turns, even after weeks of planning.

reach.learn: Whether calls about smoke from planned burns fall.

evidence.claim: Plan templates and group messages can replace building plans from scratch and calling contacts one by one.

assumptions: Boundary: from the burn request to the burn completed; the postburn report is outside.
Input contract: requests from the land manager; contacts kept by the region; fallback is phone calls.

Coordinating, deciding go or no-go, checking the start message and directing the burn keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because map, objectives, limits and crew fill from the last plan of the unit and the captain writes the rest; s4 keeps 20 for the send and calls to anyone not reached.
Neighbours read the message in about the time a call took; no added neighbour time.
research_questions: Do smoke reports to the dispatch centre fall?

incremental.description: Fire captain keeps the contact list current.

approvals.approved_version: The burn start message with burn unit, start time and the captain's contact number exactly as checked in s4c, sent once to the dispatch centre, land manager and neighbours on the burn's contact list; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most burns are on units with no earlier plan, so little fills in, and dispatch still wants a call (4.8); high: repeat units and one message as designed (10.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the fire safety codes and guidelines that apply, study and interpret them, write the permit procedure for hazardous substances, check it with the legal advisor, publish it, and brief permit officers.

steps.what: Fire captain finds the fire safety codes and guidelines that apply to the substances
Fire captain studies and interprets fire safety codes for hazardous or flammable substances
Fire captain writes the procedure and checklist for issuing permits

loop.input: The captain's interpretation notes and the texts of the applicable codes and guidelines.
loop.output: Draft procedure steps and checklist items, each with the article it relies on.
loop.check: Code checks every quoted article text appears in the current version of the code or guideline and drops items without a match. The captain reads each drafted step against their interpretation and the quoted article, and keeps it only if the article supports it; unclear items are written by the captain.
loop.stop: Stops when every item has a matching quote and the captain approves, or after two failed redrafts the captain writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning code articles into permit steps needs interpretation in prose; a search only finds the articles.

steps.what: Fire captain checks the procedure with the legal advisor
Fire captain checks the final procedure version: steps, checklist items, the legal advisor's changes and the permit team's folder
Fire captain publishes the checked procedure to the permit team: by e-mail today, as a new version in the document system after the change
Fire captain briefs permit officers on the new procedure

tasks.design: Current codes and guidelines sit in one searchable document system ({DOCS}) with versions, so the captain finds the articles that apply without searching several sites. A bounded step drafts procedure steps and checklist items from the captain's interpretation; code checks every quoted article against the current text, and the captain reads each step against the article and edits. After the legal advisor's review the captain checks the final version and publishes it to the permit team in the document system. Interpreting the codes stays with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Codes were searched on several sites and procedures written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems hold current code texts; language models draft procedure text from notes.
tasks.still_hard: Guidelines change and older procedures go out of date.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which storage rule a small business can really meet.
tasks.altitude: The captain interprets and edits instead of searching and writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether the procedure cuts questions back to the fire service.

evidence.claim: Safety regions apply PGS 15 for stored hazardous substances in permit procedures; version 1.1 dates from April 2026.
Language models can draft procedure text from notes, with quotes checked against source texts by code.

assumptions: Boundary: from the permit question to the officers briefed; issuing permits is outside.
Input contract: code texts from the publishers; fallback is searching their sites.

Interpreting codes, the legal review, the final check and briefing keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because searching several sites goes and reading stays; s3 keeps 75 because the draft fills standard items and the captain writes the steps; publishing keeps 25.
The legal advisor's time does not change.
research_questions: How many drafted items does the captain drop?

already_counted.description: Fire captain edits and approves drafted procedure items.

incremental.description: Fire captain checks procedures when a guideline changes.

approvals.approved_version: The procedure and checklist exactly as checked by the captain in s4c after the legal advisor's review, published once as a new version in the permit team's folder in the document system; any change needs a new check and version.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the document system lacks some guidelines, so searching stays in part, and most drafted items are rewritten (10.0); high: codes complete and drafts mostly kept (19.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fire captain keeps judging burns, inspecting, deciding go or no-go and interpreting codes; paper readings, typed reports, phone rounds and code searches shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A captain with more time on site and with the crew.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers
